title: Metadichol as a Coordinated Activator of Core Cellular Machinery. Part IV — One Switch for the Decoding Engine: Metadichol Coordinately Activates the Entire 40S Small-Subunit Ribosomal Protein Repertoire and Its Master Regulator c-Myc
content: Background. Metadichol® (Nano-Policosanol; Nanorx Inc.) is a nano-emulsion of food-derived very-long-chain primary alcohols (C26–C36) that acts as a Vitamin D Receptor (VDR) inverse agonist at picomolar-to-nanomolar concentrations. Prior peer-reviewed work documents its regulation of all 49 nuclear receptors, all 7 sirtuins, Toll-like receptors, the Yamanaka pluripotency factors, and—in a companion study—the complete 47-gene 60S large ribosomal subunit. The 40S small subunit is the decoding engine of the ribosome: it reads the mRNA, monitors codon–anticodon fidelity, and is built from 32 small-subunit proteins (31 RPS proteins plus the constitutive scaffold RACK1), several of which double as extraribosomal hubs in p53 surveillance (RPS7, RPS10, RPS27), NF-κB signalling (RPS3), mTORC1 sensing (RPS6), antiviral IRES translation (RPS25), and ubiquitin supply (RPS27A). Whether a single food-derived compound can coordinately regulate this entire small-subunit set—together with c-Myc, the master transcriptional driver of all ribosomal protein genes—has not been tested.Methods. Human PBMCs were isolated by Histopaque-1077 density-gradient centrifugation and treated for 24 h with Metadichol at 0.1 pg/mL, 1 pg/mL, 100 pg/mL, 1 ng/mL, and 100 ng/mL alongside untreated controls. Total RNA was extracted (TRIzol), reverse-transcribed (500 ng; PrimeScript), and 33 genes—31 RPS small-subunit genes, RACK1, and c-Myc—were quantified by SYBR-Green qRT-PCR (39 cycles; 60 °C annealing) using gene-specific validated primers. Relative expression was computed by the 2^−ΔΔCq method with GAPDH as reference.Results. Metadichol drove a strikingly coherent, non-monotonic (biphasic) response. At the lowest dose (0.1 pg/mL), 31 of 33 genes fell below control (panel mean 0.63-fold) with 9 significant suppressions; activation then rose steeply to a sharp maximum at 1 ng/mL—where 21 of 33 genes reached their individual peak and the panel mean was 2.51-fold—before partial relaxation at 100 ng/mL. At 1 ng/mL, 30 of 33 genes were significantly up-regulated and none were significantly down. The largest single responses were RPS3 (7.18×, the NF-κB co-activator), RPS16 (4.36×), RPS9 (4.09×), RPS24 (4.03×), RPS15 (3.77×), RPS28 (3.63×), RPS27 (3.57×), RPS29 (3.54×), and RPS11 (3.44×). The master regulator c-Myc was itself induced (2.76×), as was the RACK1 scaffold (1.87×). A 33×33 gene–gene correlation matrix was overwhelmingly positive (158 of 528 gene-pairs at r ≥ 0.90; none anti-correlated), and hierarchical clustering resolved one dominant co-regulated module, indicating a single shared upstream driver. By a strict criterion, 32 of 33 genes were significantly up-regulated at one or more doses; only the p53/MDM2 sentinel RPS7 was a pure low-dose suppressed gene that never reached a significant up-call.Conclusions. Metadichol produces a stoichiometrically balanced, dose-tuned activation of the entire 40S small-subunit gene set—and of c-Myc—in primary human immune cells. To our knowledge this is the first agent shown to coordinately up-regulate the complete decoding-subunit repertoire. It runs counter to the existing ribosome pharmacopeia, which is almost entirely inhibitory (mTOR inhibitors, RNA Pol I inhibitors), and is the inverse of the selective, imbalanced RPS changes that drive ribosomopathies (Diamond–Blackfan anemia, 5q- MDS). The behaviour instead resembles the coordinated biogenesis program of pluripotent and regenerating cells, in which c-Myc switches the ribosomal-protein regulon back on. Together with the companion 60S findings, these results position Metadichol as the first coordinated, balanced transcriptional activator of complete translational capacity, with implications for ribosomopathy, iPSC reprogramming, immune function, and ageing biology.
